ground_truth_diagnosis: RecommendationService pods are OOMKilled (exit 137) because -Xmx1024m lets the JVM heap alone use the entire 1Gi container limit. Metaspace, thread stacks and GC structures have no room, so the kernel sends SIGKILL before the JVM can throw an OutOfMemoryError. Fix: replace -Xmx1024m with -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75.0 in the deployment manifest.

expected_evidence_mapping.claim: RecommendationService's OOMKilled code is registered as Container Memory (SEV-3, Recommendations-Team) with a 1024 MiB memory limit and a 1024 MB JVM max heap.
A heap sized to the full container limit leaves no room for non-heap JVM memory, so the kernel kills the container before any Java error is logged.

The liveness probe starts at 10 seconds and fails with connection refused, so the kubelet kills the container at about 25 seconds, and the next start fails the same way. Fix: add a startupProbe on /healthz with failureThreshold 30 and periodSeconds 5.

user_input: Every InventoryService pod restarted at the same time about 10 minutes ago. The events say the liveness probe timed out, not connection refused. InventoryDB latency has been high since then. Why did all pods restart together?
ground_truth_diagnosis: The InventoryService liveness probe on /healthz also queries InventoryDB. When the database is slow, every pod fails liveness at once, so the kubelet restarts them together and a database slowdown becomes a full outage. Fix: keep the liveness probe shallow (check only that the process responds) and move the InventoryDB check into the readiness probe.

expected_evidence_mapping.claim: The CrashLoopBackOff code for InventoryService is registered with a liveness failure threshold of 3.
The liveness probe checks InventoryDB as well, so a slow database fails every pod's liveness check at the same time.

ground_truth_diagnosis: ImageService pods are being evicted because failed resize jobs leave temporary files in /tmp, which is backed by node ephemeral storage, and never delete them. The node disk fills past the kubelet's 10% free threshold, and the kubelet evicts pods, starting with the largest consumer.

expected_evidence_mapping.claim: The Evicted code for ImageService is registered as Node Resource Pressure (SEV-3, Media-Team) with a 10% nodefs eviction threshold.
Temporary files from failed resizes are not deleted, so they fill the node disk over days until the kubelet evicts pods.

user_input: Our checkout pods on worker-node-3 keep getting Evicted even though their own usage looks fine, and nothing in our service changed. Which workload is filling the node's disk, and why do unrelated pods get killed?
ground_truth_diagnosis: ImageService is filling the node's ephemeral storage with temporary files from failed resizes. Because ImageService has no ephemeral-storage limits, one pod can consume the whole node disk, so the kubelet evicts pods across the node, including unrelated checkout pods. Fix: set ephemeral-storage requests and limits on image-service (request 2Gi, limit 4Gi) and delete temporary files in a finally block so failed resizes do not leak them.

expected_evidence_mapping.claim: The Evicted code for ImageService is registered as Node Resource Pressure with a 10% nodefs eviction threshold.
Without ephemeral-storage limits, one pod can consume the whole node disk, so the kubelet evicts pods across the node instead of only the offending pod.
